sentences.zh: 賀世賢，榆林衛人。

translations.literal: He Shixian was a native of Yulin Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He Shixian was from Yulin Guard.

sentences.zh: 少為廝養，後從軍，積功至沈陽遊擊，遷義州參將。

translations.literal: In youth he was a household servant; later he entered the army, and through accumulated merit rose to roaming-brigade commander at Shenyang, then was transferred to assistant commander at Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he had been a household servant, but he later joined the army and, through accumulated merit, rose to roaming-brigade commander at Shenyang and then to assistant commander at Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十六年七月，清河被圍，副將鄒儲賢固守。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the forty-sixth year of Wanli, Qinghe was besieged, and Vice Commander Zou Chuxian held firm in defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Wanli 46, Qinghe came under siege, and Vice Commander Zou Chuxian mounted a stubborn defense.

sentences.zh: 城破，率親丁鏖戰城南，與參將張俱死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he led his personal retainers in fierce fighting south of the city and died together with Assistant Commander Zhang Ying.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he led his personal retainers in a desperate fight south of the walls and perished together with Assistant Commander Zhang Ying.

sentences.zh: 部將二十人、兵民萬余殲焉。

translations.literal: Twenty subordinate officers and more than ten thousand soldiers and civilians were annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty subordinate officers and more than ten thousand soldiers and civilians were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 世賢駐叆陽，聞變，疾馳出塞，得首功百五十有四級，進副總兵。

translations.literal: Shixian was stationed at Aiyang; hearing of the disaster, he raced out beyond the pass and took one hundred fifty-four enemy heads, and was promoted to vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian was stationed at Aiyang. When he heard what had happened, he galloped out beyond the pass and claimed one hundred fifty-four enemy heads, earning promotion to vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 明年，楊鎬四路出師。

translations.literal: The next year Yang Hao marched out by four routes.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yang Hao launched his four-route campaign.

sentences.zh: 世賢副李如柏出清河。

translations.literal: Shixian served as deputy to Li Rubo in the advance out of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian served under Li Rubo on the Qinghe route.

sentences.zh: 劉綎深入中伏，勸如柏往救，不從，綎遂覆歿。

translations.literal: Liu Ting advanced deep and fell into an ambush; Shixian urged Rubo to go to his rescue, but Rubo would not comply, and Ting was utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ting pushed deep into enemy territory and walked into an ambush. Shixian urged Rubo to go to his relief, but Rubo refused, and Ting's force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 尋擢都督僉事，充總兵官，駐虎皮驛。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Commissioner-in-chief of the Chief Military Commission and appointed regional commander, stationed at Hupi Post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice commissioner of the Chief Military Commission and appointed regional commander, with his headquarters at Hupi Post.

sentences.zh: 鐵嶺被圍，世賢馳援，城已破，邀獲首功百余級。

translations.literal: When Tieling was besieged, Shixian raced to its relief; though the city had already fallen, he intercepted the enemy and took more than a hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: When Tieling came under siege, Shixian hurried to its relief. The city had already fallen, but he intercepted the enemy and took more than a hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 泰昌元年九月連戰灰山、撫安堡，獲首功二百有奇。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Taichang he fought repeatedly at Huishan and Fu'an Fort and took more than two hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Taichang 1 he fought repeatedly at Huishan and Fu'an Fort and claimed more than two hundred enemy heads.

sentences.zh: 當是時，四方宿將鱗集遼左，率縮朒不敢戰，獨世賢數角鬥有功，同列多忌之。

translations.literal: At that time veteran generals from all quarters gathered thick as scales in eastern Liaodong, and for the most part shrank back and dared not fight; only Shixian repeatedly engaged the enemy with merit, and his peers were much jealous of him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time veteran generals from every quarter had gathered in eastern Liaodong, yet most shrank from battle. Shixian alone fought the enemy again and again with real success, and his peers grew jealous.

sentences.zh: 移鎮沈陽。

translations.literal: He was transferred to command at Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 經略袁應泰下納降令。

translations.literal: The frontier commissioner Yuan Yingtai issued an order to accept surrenders.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier Commissioner Yuan Yingtai issued an order to accept surrenders.

sentences.zh: 廣寧總兵李光榮疑世賢所納多，以狀聞。

translations.literal: Guangning regional commander Li Guangrong suspected that those Shixian had accepted were too many and reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Guangning regional commander Li Guangrong suspected that Shixian had taken in too many defectors and reported the matter upward.

sentences.zh: 巡撫薛國用亦奏三可慮，兵部尚書崔景榮請拒勿納，而置己納於他所。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Xue Guoyong also memorialized three grounds for concern; Minister of War Cui Jingrong asked that no more be accepted and that those already accepted be placed elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Xue Guoyong also memorialized three grounds for concern, and Minister of War Cui Jingrong urged that no more defectors be accepted and that those already taken in be moved elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 然世賢所納卒不可散，同列遂謗其有異志。

translations.literal: Yet those Shixian had accepted could in the end not be dispersed, and his peers then slandered him as harboring disloyal intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the men Shixian had accepted could not be sent away, and his peers began to slander him as disloyal.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年三月，我大清以重兵薄沈陽。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Tianqi, Our Great Qing pressed Shenyang with a heavy force.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Tianqi 1, the Great Qing pressed Shenyang with a heavy army.

sentences.zh: 世賢及總兵尤世功掘塹浚壕，樹大木為柵，列楯車火器木石，環城設兵，守城法甚具。

translations.literal: Shixian and regional commander You Shigong dug ditches and deepened moats, set up great timbers as palisades, arrayed shield-carts, firearms, timber, and stones, and posted troops all around the wall—the methods of defense were very complete.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian and regional commander You Shigong dug ditches, deepened the moats, erected palisades of great timbers, lined up shield-carts, firearms, beams, and stones, and posted troops all around the walls. Their defensive preparations were thorough.

sentences.zh: 大清先以數十騎來偵，世功兵躡之，殺四人。

translations.literal: The Great Qing first sent several dozen horsemen to reconnoiter; Shigong's troops pursued them and killed four.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing first sent several dozen horsemen to scout the defenses. Shigong's men pursued them and killed four.

sentences.zh: 世賢勇而輕，嗜酒。

translations.literal: Shixian was brave but rash and fond of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian was brave but reckless and fond of drink.

sentences.zh: 旦日飲酒，率親丁千，出城逆擊，期盡敵而反。

translations.literal: One morning after drinking wine, he led a thousand personal retainers out of the city to meet the enemy head-on, intending to destroy them utterly and return.
translations.idiomatic: One morning, after drinking, he led a thousand personal retainers out of the city to meet the enemy head-on, intending to destroy them utterly and return.

sentences.zh: 大清兵佯敗，世賢乘銳進。

translations.literal: The Qing troops feigned defeat, and Shixian pressed forward on their heels while still sharp.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing troops feigned a retreat, and Shixian pressed forward while his men were still fresh.

sentences.zh: 倏精騎四合，世賢戰且卻，抵西門，身被十四矢。

translations.literal: Suddenly elite cavalry closed in on all sides; Shixian fought while retreating until he reached the west gate, his body struck by fourteen arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly elite cavalry closed in on every side. Shixian fought his way back to the west gate with fourteen arrows in his body.

sentences.zh: 城中聞世賢敗，各鳥獸竄，而降丁復叛，斷城外吊橋。

translations.literal: Within the city, hearing that Shixian had been defeated, men scattered like birds and beasts; surrendered troops rebelled again and cut the drawbridge outside the wall.
translations.idiomatic: When the city heard that Shixian had been beaten, the garrison broke apart in panic. Surrendered troops rebelled again and cut the drawbridge outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 或勸世賢走遼陽，曰：「吾為大將，不能存城，何面目見袁經略乎！

translations.literal: Some urged Shixian to flee to Liaoyang. He said, "As a supreme commander, if I cannot preserve the city, what face have I to see Commissioner Yuan?"
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Shixian to flee to Liaoyang. He said, "I am the supreme commander. If I cannot hold the city, what face have I to show Commissioner Yuan?"

sentences.zh: 」揮鐵鞭馳突圍中，擊殺數人，中矢墜馬而死。

translations.literal: " He flourished an iron whip and charged through the encirclement, striking down several men, then was hit by arrows, fell from his horse, and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He flourished an iron whip and charged into the encirclement, killing several men before arrows brought him down from his horse.

sentences.zh: 世功引兵援，亦戰死。

translations.literal: Shigong led troops to his relief and also died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shigong led troops to his relief and also died fighting.

sentences.zh: 世功亦榆林人。

translations.literal: Shigong was also a native of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Shigong was also from Yulin.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，舉武鄉試，歷沈陽遊擊。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign he passed the military provincial examination and served through the post of roaming-brigade commander at Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he passed the military provincial examination and eventually served as roaming-brigade commander at Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 張承蔭之敗也，世功脫歸，坐褫職。

translations.literal: When Zhang Chengyin was defeated, Shigong escaped back and was punished by dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Chengyin's defeat, Shigong made his way back alive but was stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 經略楊鎬言其身負重傷，才堪策勵，乃補武精營遊擊。

translations.literal: Commissioner Yang Hao said that though he bore serious wounds, his talent was fit to be roused, and he was reappointed roaming-brigade commander of the Martial Elite Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Yang Hao argued that despite his serious wounds, his talent was worth encouraging, and he was reappointed roaming-brigade commander of the Martial Elite Battalion.

sentences.zh: 鎬四路出師，世功隸李如柏麾下，得全。

translations.literal: When Hao marched out by four routes, Shigong served under Li Rubo and came through intact.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao launched the four-route campaign, Shigong served under Li Rubo and came through unscathed.

sentences.zh: 尋以副總兵守沈陽。

translations.literal: Soon he was made vice commander-in-chief to defend Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed vice commander-in-chief to defend Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 熊廷弼代鎬，愛其才，與副將朱萬良並倚任。

translations.literal: Xiong Tingbi replaced Hao, valued his talent, and relied on him together with Vice Commander Zhu Wanliang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiong Tingbi replaced Hao, he valued Shigong's talent and relied on him together with Vice Commander Zhu Wanliang.

sentences.zh: 廷弼罷，袁應泰代，議三路出師，用為總兵官。

translations.literal: When Tingbi was dismissed, Yuan Yingtai replaced him; as a three-route advance was discussed, Shigong was appointed regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Tingbi was dismissed, Yuan Yingtai replaced him. When a three-route advance was planned, Shigong was appointed regional commander.

sentences.zh: 未行，而沈陽被兵，死於戰。

translations.literal: Before he could march, Shenyang came under attack and he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could march out, Shenyang came under attack and he died in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈少保、左都督，增世蔭三級，再蔭指揮僉事，世襲，賜祭葬，建祠曰「湣忠」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian and Left Chief Commander, his family's hereditary privilege was raised three grades, and he received a second enfeoffment as battalion commander with hereditary succession, sacrificial rites, and burial honors; a shrine was built called "Loyal in Sorrow."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian and Left Chief Commander. His family's hereditary privilege was raised three grades, he received a second enfeoffment as battalion commander with hereditary succession, and he was granted sacrificial rites and state burial. A shrine called "Loyal in Sorrow" was built in his honor.

sentences.zh: 世賢既歿，或疑其叛降，恤典故不及。

translations.literal: After Shixian died, some suspected he had defected and surrendered, and the precedents for posthumous favors did not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: After Shixian's death, some suspected he had defected, and the usual posthumous honors were withheld.

sentences.zh: 四川副使車樸為訟冤，格眾議不果。

translations.literal: Sichuan Vice Commissioner Che Pu pleaded his innocence, but contrary opinion blocked the effort.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan Vice Commissioner Che Pu pleaded his case, but opposition blocked the effort.

sentences.zh: 童仲揆，南京人。

translations.literal: Tong Zhongkui was a native of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Zhongkui was from Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 舉武會試，歷都指揮，掌四川都司。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan military examination, served through the post of regional commander, and directed the Sichuan Regional Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan military examination, rose through the post of regional commander, and directed the Sichuan Regional Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 萬歷末，擢副總兵，督川兵援遼，與同官陳策並充援剿總兵官。

translations.literal: At the end of Wanli he was promoted vice commander-in-chief, supervised Sichuan troops in relief of Liaodong, and together with his colleague Chen Ce was appointed relief-and-suppression regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Wanli reign he was promoted vice commander-in-chief to lead Sichuan troops to Liaodong, and he and his colleague Chen Ce were both appointed relief-and-suppression regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 熹宗初立，經略袁應泰招蒙古諸部，處之遼、瀋二城。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong had just ascended, Commissioner Yuan Yingtai summoned the Mongol tribes and settled them in the two cities of Liaoyang and Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Emperor Xizong ascended the throne, Commissioner Yuan Yingtai summoned Mongol tribes and settled them in Liaoyang and Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 仲揆力諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Zhongkui remonstrated forcefully, but his advice was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkui remonstrated forcefully, but his advice went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 明年，天啟改元，應泰欲城清河、撫順。

translations.literal: The next year, with the change of reign title to Tianqi, Yingtai wished to fortify Qinghe and Fushun.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, with the new Tianqi reign, Yingtai proposed fortifying Qinghe and Fushun.

sentences.zh: 議三路出師，用大將十人，各將兵萬余，仲揆、策當其二。

translations.literal: A three-route advance was discussed, employing ten great generals, each leading more than ten thousand men; Zhongkui and Ce were to hold two of the routes.
translations.idiomatic: A three-route advance was planned with ten senior generals, each commanding more than ten thousand men. Zhongkui and Ce were assigned two of the routes.

sentences.zh: 未行，而大清兵已逼沈陽。

translations.literal: Before they could march, Qing troops were already pressing Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could march out, Qing forces were already pressing Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 兩人馳救，次渾河。

translations.literal: The two men raced to the rescue and halted at the Hun River.
translations.idiomatic: The two men hurried to the relief and halted at the Hun River.

sentences.zh: 遊擊周敦吉曰：「事急矣，請直抵沈陽，與城中兵夾擊，可以成功。

translations.literal: Roaming-brigade commander Zhou Dunji said, "The situation is urgent. Please go straight to Shenyang and strike the enemy from both sides together with the troops in the city—success can be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: Roaming-brigade commander Zhou Dunji said, "The situation is desperate. Go straight to Shenyang and strike the enemy from both sides with the troops inside the city. That is how we can win."

sentences.zh: 」已，聞沈陽陷，諸將皆憤曰：「我輩不能救沈，在此三年何為！

translations.literal: " Presently, hearing that Shenyang had fallen, the generals all said in anger, "If we cannot save Shenyang, what have we been doing here for three years!"
translations.idiomatic: " Soon they heard that Shenyang had fallen. The generals cried out in anger, "If we cannot save Shenyang, what have we been doing here for three years?"

sentences.zh: 」敦吉固請與石砫都司秦邦屏先渡河，營橋北，仲揆、策及副將戚金、參將張名世統浙兵三千營橋南。

translations.literal: " Dunji urgently asked to cross the river first with Qin Bangping, commander of the Shizhu garrison, and encamp north of the bridge, while Zhongkui, Ce, Vice Commander Qi Jin, and Assistant Commander Zhang Mingshi commanded three thousand Zhejiang troops and encamped south of the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: " Dunji pressed to cross the river first with Qin Bangping, commander of the Shizhu garrison, and encamp north of the bridge, while Zhongkui, Ce, Vice Commander Qi Jin, and Assistant Commander Zhang Mingshi took three thousand Zhejiang troops and encamped south of it.

sentences.zh: 邦屏結陣未就，大清兵來攻，卻復前者三，諸軍遂敗。

translations.literal: Bangping had not yet finished forming his battle line when Qing troops came to attack; they drove back the front ranks three times, and the armies were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Bangping had not yet finished forming his line when Qing troops attacked, drove back the front ranks three times, and broke the army.

sentences.zh: 敦吉、邦屏及參將吳文傑、守備雷安民等皆死。

translations.literal: Dunji, Bangping, Assistant Commander Wu Wenjie, Garrison Commander Lei Anmin, and others all died.
translations.idiomatic: Dunji, Bangping, Assistant Commander Wu Wenjie, Garrison Commander Lei Anmin, and others all fell.

sentences.zh: 他將走入浙兵營，被圍數匝。

translations.literal: The other generals ran into the Zhejiang camp and were surrounded layer upon layer.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals fled into the Zhejiang camp and were surrounded on every side.

sentences.zh: 副將朱萬良、姜弼不救，及圍急始前，一戰即敗走。

translations.literal: Vice Commanders Zhu Wanliang and Jiang Bi did not go to their relief; only when the encirclement grew desperate did they advance, and after one battle they were routed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commanders Zhu Wanliang and Jiang Bi held back until the encirclement was desperate, then advanced once, were beaten at once, and fled.

sentences.zh: 大清兵盡銳攻浙營。

translations.literal: Qing troops attacked the Zhejiang camp with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing threw their full strength against the Zhejiang camp.

sentences.zh: 營中用火器，多殺傷。

translations.literal: Within the camp firearms were used and many were killed and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The camp answered with firearms and inflicted heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 火藥盡，短兵接，遂大潰。

translations.literal: When gunpowder was exhausted they closed at close quarters, and then there was a great rout.
translations.idiomatic: When the gunpowder ran out they closed at close quarters, and the army broke completely.

sentences.zh: 策先戰死，仲揆將奔，金止之，乃還兵鬥。

translations.literal: Ce was the first to die in battle; Zhongkui was about to flee, but Jin stopped him, and he turned his troops back to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Ce was killed first. Zhongkui was about to flee, but Qi Jin stopped him, and he turned his men back to fight.

sentences.zh: 力盡矢竭，揮刀殺十七人。

translations.literal: His strength spent and his arrows exhausted, he swung his blade and killed seventeen men.
translations.idiomatic: When his strength was spent and his arrows gone, he swung his blade and killed seventeen men.

sentences.zh: 大清兵萬矢齊發，仲揆與金、名世及都司袁見龍、鄧起龍等並死焉。

translations.literal: Qing troops loosed ten thousand arrows together; Zhongkui, Jin, Mingshi, and battalion commanders Yuan Jianlong, Deng Qilong, and others all died.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand Qing arrows flew at once. Zhongkui, Jin, Mingshi, and battalion commanders Yuan Jianlong, Deng Qilong, and others all fell.

sentences.zh: 萬良既遁，經略將斬之，乞勚罪自效。

translations.literal: Wanliang having fled, the commissioner was about to execute him, but he begged to atone for his fault by meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: After Wanliang fled, the commissioner was about to execute him, but he begged to redeem himself with meritorious service.

sentences.zh: 及遼陽被攻，果陷陣死。

translations.literal: When Liaoyang came under attack, he indeed died in the breach.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaoyang came under attack, he did die in the breach as he had promised.

sentences.zh: 自遼左用兵，將士率望風奔潰，獨此以萬余人當數萬眾。

translations.literal: Since warfare began in eastern Liaodong, officers and soldiers for the most part fled at sight of the wind; only here did more than ten thousand men face several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Since the war in eastern Liaodong began, officers and soldiers had usually fled at the first sign of danger. Here alone more than ten thousand men faced several tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 雖力絀而覆，時鹹壯之。

translations.literal: Though their strength was exhausted and they were destroyed, at the time all admired their valor.
translations.idiomatic: Though they were overwhelmed in the end, contemporaries admired their courage.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈策少保、左都督，增世蔭三級，再蔭本衛指揮僉事，世襲，賜祭葬，建祠曰：「湣忠」。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Ce was posthumously granted Junior Guardian and Left Chief Commander; his family's hereditary privilege was raised three grades, with a second enfeoffment as battalion commander of his original guard with hereditary succession; sacrificial rites and burial honors were granted, and a shrine was built called "Loyal in Sorrow."
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, Ce was posthumously made Junior Guardian and Left Chief Commander. His family's hereditary privilege was raised three grades, he received a second enfeoffment as battalion commander of his original guard with hereditary succession, and he was granted sacrificial rites and state burial. A shrine called "Loyal in Sorrow" was built in his honor.

sentences.zh: 仲揆贈都督同知，增世蔭三級，祀祀。

translations.literal: Zhongkui was posthumously granted Vice Commissioner-in-chief of the Chief Military Commission, his family's hereditary privilege was raised three grades, and he received sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkui was posthumously made Vice Commissioner of the Chief Military Commission, his family's hereditary privilege was raised three grades, and he was granted sacrificial honors.

sentences.zh: 金、起龍贈都督僉事，增世蔭三級，附祀。

translations.literal: Jin and Qilong were posthumously granted Vice Commissioner-in-chief, their families' hereditary privileges were raised three grades, and they received attendant sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Qilong were posthumously made Vice Commissioners, their families' hereditary privileges were raised three grades, and they were granted attendant sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 名世先有罪系獄，尚書薛三才薦其善火器，命從征立功。

translations.literal: Mingshi had earlier been guilty and imprisoned; Minister Xue Sancai recommended his skill with firearms, and he was ordered to follow the campaign and earn merit.
translations.idiomatic: Mingshi had earlier been imprisoned for an offense, but Minister Xue Sancai recommended his skill with firearms, and he was ordered to join the campaign and earn merit.

sentences.zh: 文傑亦先褫職。

translations.literal: Wenjie had also earlier been dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjie had also been stripped of office earlier.

sentences.zh: 及死，並得復官，贈三級，增世蔭二級。

translations.literal: When they died, all had their offices restored, were granted three grades posthumously, and their families' hereditary privileges were raised two grades.
translations.idiomatic: When they died, all had their offices restored, received posthumous promotion of three grades, and their families' hereditary privileges were raised two grades.

sentences.zh: 見龍等皆予贈蔭，他副將至把總戰死者百二十余人，贈蔭有差。

translations.literal: Jianlong and the others all received posthumous honors and enfeoffments; of the other vice commanders down to platoon leaders who died in battle, more than one hundred twenty persons received honors and enfeoffments in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Jianlong and the others all received posthumous honors and enfeoffments. More than one hundred twenty other officers from vice commander down to platoon leader who died in battle received honors in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 敦吉，先為四川永寧參將。

translations.literal: Dunji had earlier served as assistant commander at Yongning in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dunji had earlier served as assistant commander at Yongning in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 永寧宣撫奢效忠卒，子崇明幼，其妻奢世統與妾奢世續爭印，相攻者十余年。

translations.literal: When Pacification Commissioner She Xiaozhong of Yongning died, his son Chongming was young; his wife She Shitong and concubine She Shixu fought over the seal, attacking each other for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongning Pacification Commissioner She Xiaozhong died, his son Chongming was still young. His wife She Shitong and his concubine She Shixu fought over the official seal and had been at war with each other for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 後崇明襲職，世續猶匿印不予。

translations.literal: Later Chongming succeeded to the office, but Shixu still hid the seal and would not hand it over.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chongming succeeded to the office, but Shixu still kept the seal hidden and refused to surrender it.

sentences.zh: 都司張神武與敦吉謀，盡掠其積聚子女，擒世續以歸。

translations.literal: Battalion commander Zhang Shenwu plotted with Dunji, plundered all their accumulated goods, women, and children, and seized Shixu and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: Battalion commander Zhang Shenwu plotted with Dunji to plunder all their stored wealth, women, and children, seize Shixu, and bring him back.

sentences.zh: 其部目閻宗傳怒，以求主母為名，大掠永寧、赤水、普市、麾尼，數百里成兵墟。

translations.literal: Their subordinate officer Yan Zongchuan was enraged; under the pretext of seeking the mistress of the house, he ravaged Yongning, Chishui, Pushi, and Huini, and for several hundred li the land became a wasteland of war.
translations.idiomatic: Their subordinate Yan Zongchuan flew into a rage and, claiming he was seeking the lady of the house, ravaged Yongning, Chishui, Pushi, and Huini until hundreds of li of country lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 事聞，敦吉、神武並論死。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Dunji and Shenwu were both sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, Dunji and Shenwu were both sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 遼東告警，命敦吉從軍自效，及是鏖戰死，贈恤如制。

translations.literal: When Liaodong raised the alarm, Dunji was ordered to follow the army and redeem himself; at this time he died in fierce battle, and posthumous favors were granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaodong came under threat, Dunji was ordered to join the army and redeem himself. He died fighting at the Hun River, and posthumous honors were granted according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 神武，新建人。

translations.literal: Shenwu was a native of Xinjian.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu was from Xinjian.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中舉武會試第一。

translations.literal: During Wanli he took first place in the metropolitan military examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he took first place in the metropolitan military examination.

sentences.zh: 授四川都司僉書。

translations.literal: He was appointed secretary of the Sichuan Regional Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed secretary of the Sichuan Regional Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 既論死，遼左兵興，用經略袁應泰薦，詔諭從征立功。

translations.literal: After he had been sentenced to death, warfare arose in eastern Liaodong; on the recommendation of Commissioner Yuan Yingtai, an edict ordered him to follow the campaign and earn merit.
translations.idiomatic: After his death sentence, war broke out in eastern Liaodong. On Commissioner Yuan Yingtai's recommendation, an edict ordered him to join the campaign and earn merit.

sentences.zh: 神武率親丁二百四十余，疾馳至廣寧。

translations.literal: Shenwu led more than two hundred forty personal retainers and raced to Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu led more than two hundred forty personal retainers and raced to Guangning.

sentences.zh: 會遼陽已失，巡撫薛國用固留之，不可，曰：「奉命守遼陽，非守廣寧也。

translations.literal: It happened that Liaoyang had already fallen; Grand Coordinator Xue Guoyong firmly detained him, but he would not stay, saying, "I was ordered to defend Liaoyang, not to defend Guangning."
translations.idiomatic: Liaoyang had already fallen. Grand Coordinator Xue Guoyong tried hard to keep him, but he refused, saying, "I was ordered to defend Liaoyang, not Guangning."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「遼陽歿矣，若何之？

translations.literal: " He was told, "Liaoyang is lost—where will you go?"
translations.idiomatic: " They said, "Liaoyang is gone. Where will you go?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「將以殲敵。

translations.literal: " He said, "To destroy the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "To destroy the enemy."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「二百人能殲敵乎？

translations.literal: " He was asked, "Can two hundred men destroy the enemy?"
translations.idiomatic: " They asked, "Can two hundred men destroy the enemy?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「不能，則死之。

translations.literal: " He said, "If not, then die."
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "If not, then we die."

sentences.zh: 」前至遼河，遇逃卒十余萬。

translations.literal: " He advanced to the Liao River and encountered more than one hundred thousand fleeing soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: " He advanced to the Liao River and met more than one hundred thousand fleeing soldiers.

sentences.zh: 神武以忠義激其帥，欲與還戰，帥不從。

translations.literal: Shenwu stirred their commander with talk of loyalty and righteousness and wished to return with them to fight, but the commander would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu tried to rouse their commander with appeals to loyalty and urged a return to battle, but the commander refused.

sentences.zh: 乃獨率所部渡河，抵首山，去遼陽十七里而軍。

translations.literal: He then led his own troops alone across the river, reached Shoushan, and encamped seventeen li from Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his own men across the river alone, reached Shoushan, and encamped seventeen li from Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 將士不食已一日，遇大清兵，疾呼奮擊，孤軍無援，盡歿於陣。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers had not eaten for a full day; they met Qing troops, cried out and struck fiercely, but as a lone army without relief all perished on the field.
translations.idiomatic: His men had not eaten for a full day. They met Qing troops, charged with a shout, and as an isolated force without relief they were wiped out on the field.

sentences.zh: 監軍御史方震孺繪神武像，率將士羅拜，為文祭之。

translations.literal: Supervising censor Fang Zhenru painted Shenwu's portrait, led the officers and soldiers in bowing in array, and composed a text to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Fang Zhenru had Shenwu's portrait painted, led the officers and soldiers in a formal bow, and composed a funeral text in his honor.

sentences.zh: 詔贈都督僉事，世蔭千戶，立祠祀之。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Vice Commissioner-in-chief, hereditary enfeoffment as chiliarch, and a shrine was built to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Vice Commissioner, granted his family a hereditary chiliarch enfeoffment, and ordered a shrine built in his honor.

sentences.zh: 又有楊宗業、梁仲善者，皆援遼總兵官。

translations.literal: There were also Yang Zongye and Liang Zhongshan, both regional commanders sent to relieve Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Yang Zongye and Liang Zhongshan, both regional commanders sent to relieve Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 宗業歷鎮浙江、山西。

translations.literal: Zongye had successively commanded in Zhejiang and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zongye had previously commanded in Zhejiang and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 楊鎬四路敗後，命提兵赴援，至是父子並戰死。

translations.literal: After Yang Hao's defeat on the four routes, he was ordered to lead troops to the relief; at this time father and son both died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Hao's defeat on the four routes, he was ordered to lead troops to the relief. At Liaoyang he and his son both died fighting.

sentences.zh: 仲善亦戰死遼陽城下。

translations.literal: Zhongshan also died in battle below the walls of Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan also died fighting below the walls of Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 宗業贈都督同知，世蔭千戶；

translations.literal: Zongye was posthumously granted Vice Commissioner-in-chief of the Chief Military Commission and hereditary enfeoffment as chiliarch;
translations.idiomatic: Zongye was posthumously made Vice Commissioner of the Chief Military Commission and granted a hereditary chiliarch enfeoffment;

sentences.zh: 仲善贈都督僉事，增世蔭三級。

translations.literal: Zhongshan was posthumously granted Vice Commissioner-in-chief, and his family's hereditary privilege was raised three grades.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan was posthumously made Vice Commissioner, and his family's hereditary privilege was raised three grades.

sentences.zh: 並從祠附祀。

translations.literal: Both received attendant sacrifice at the shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Both were granted attendant sacrifice at the shrine.

sentences.zh: 羅一貫，甘州衛人。

translations.literal: Luo Yiguan was a native of Ganzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yiguan was from Ganzhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 以參將守西平堡。

translations.literal: As assistant commander he defended Xiping Fort.
translations.idiomatic: As assistant commander he defended Xiping Fort.

sentences.zh: 遼陽陷，西平地最沖，一貫悉力捍禦。

translations.literal: When Liaoyang fell, Xiping's terrain was the most exposed; Yiguan defended with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: After Liaoyang fell, Xiping stood on the most exposed ground, and Yiguan defended it with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 巡撫王化貞言於朝，加副總兵。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Wang Huazhen reported to court, and he was promoted to vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Wang Huazhen reported to court, and Yiguan was promoted to vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時化貞駐廣寧，經略熊廷弼駐右屯，總兵劉渠以二萬人守鎮武，祁秉忠以萬人守閭陽，而一貫帥三千人守西平。

translations.literal: At that time Huazhen was stationed at Guangning, Commissioner Xiong Tingbi at You Tun, regional commander Liu Qu held Zhenwu with twenty thousand men, Qi Bingzhong held Lüyang with ten thousand, and Yiguan commanded three thousand men at Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Huazhen was stationed at Guangning, Commissioner Xiong Tingbi at You Tun, regional commander Liu Qu held Zhenwu with twenty thousand men, Qi Bingzhong held Lüyang with ten thousand, and Yiguan commanded three thousand at Xiping.

sentences.zh: 已，定議，各繕隍堅壘，急則互相援，違者必誅。

translations.literal: Presently an agreement was fixed: each was to repair moats and strengthen ramparts; in emergency they would aid one another, and violators would certainly be executed.
translations.idiomatic: An agreement was then fixed: each post was to repair its defenses, aid the others in an emergency, and face execution for disobedience.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，大清兵西渡河，經撫戒勿輕戰。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Qing troops crossed the river westward; the commissioner and coordinator warned against fighting lightly.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Qing troops crossed the river to the west. The frontier officials warned against rash engagement.

sentences.zh: 兵漸近，參將黑雲鶴出擊。

translations.literal: As the enemy drew nearer, Assistant Commander Hei Yunhe went out to attack.
translations.idiomatic: As the enemy drew nearer, Assistant Commander Hei Yunhe went out to attack.

sentences.zh: 一貫止之，不從。

translations.literal: Yiguan stopped him, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan tried to stop him, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 明日，雲鶴戰敗，奔還城，追兵殲焉。

translations.literal: The next day Yunhe was defeated in battle, fled back to the city, and the pursuing troops annihilated him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yunhe was beaten, fled back toward the city, and the pursuers wiped him out.

sentences.zh: 一貫憑城固拒，用炮擊傷者無算。

translations.literal: Yiguan relied on the walls and held firm in refusal; with cannon he struck down countless wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan held the walls and refused to yield. His cannon inflicted countless casualties.

sentences.zh: 大清樹旗招降，且遣使來說，一貫不從。

translations.literal: The Qing raised banners to summon surrender and also sent envoys to persuade him; Yiguan would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing raised surrender banners and sent envoys to persuade him, but Yiguan refused.

sentences.zh: 又明日，騎益眾，環城力攻。

translations.literal: On the next day cavalry grew more numerous and pressed the attack all around the walls.
translations.idiomatic: The next day more cavalry arrived and pressed the attack all around the walls.

sentences.zh: 一貫流矢中目，不能戰。

translations.literal: Yiguan was struck in the eye by a stray arrow and could not fight.
translations.idiomatic: A stray arrow struck Yiguan in the eye, and he could no longer fight.

sentences.zh: 火藥矢石盡，乃北面再拜，曰：「臣力竭矣。

translations.literal: When gunpowder, arrows, and stones were exhausted, he bowed twice facing north and said, "Your servant's strength is spent."
translations.idiomatic: When gunpowder, arrows, and stones were gone, he bowed twice toward the north and said, "Your servant's strength is spent."

sentences.zh: 」遂自剄。

translations.literal: " He then cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: " He then cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 都司陳尚仁、王崇信亦死之。

translations.literal: Battalion commanders Chen Shangren and Wang Chongxin also died with him.
translations.idiomatic: Battalion commanders Chen Shangren and Wang Chongxin died with him.

sentences.zh: 化貞知城未下，信遊擊孫得功語，盡發廣寧兵。

translations.literal: Huazhen, knowing the city had not yet fallen, believed the words of roaming-brigade commander Sun Degong and sent out all the Guangning troops.
translations.idiomatic: Huazhen, believing the city had not yet fallen, trusted roaming-brigade commander Sun Degong and sent out all the Guangning troops.

sentences.zh: 以得功及中軍遊擊祖大壽為前鋒，令會秉忠赴援，廷弼亦遣使督渠進戰，遇大清兵於平陽。

translations.literal: He made Degong and central-army roaming-brigade commander Zu Dashou the vanguard, ordered them to join Bingzhong in going to the relief, and Tingbi also sent envoys to urge Qu forward to battle; they met Qing troops at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He made Degong and central-army roaming-brigade commander Zu Dashou the vanguard, ordered them to join Bingzhong in relief, and Tingbi also sent envoys to urge Qu forward. They met Qing troops at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 得功懷異志，欲引去。

translations.literal: Degong harbored disloyal intent and wished to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Degong harbored treacherous intent and wished to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 乃分兵為左右翼，稍卻，推渠、秉忠前。

translations.literal: He then divided the troops into left and right wings, drew back slightly, and pushed Qu and Bingzhong forward.
translations.idiomatic: He divided the army into left and right wings, drew back slightly, and pushed Qu and Bingzhong to the front.

sentences.zh: 渠等力戰，頗有殺傷。

translations.literal: Qu and the others fought fiercely and inflicted considerable killing and wounding.
translations.idiomatic: Qu and the others fought hard and inflicted heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 得功及副將鮑承先走，後軍見之亦奔，遂大潰。

translations.literal: Degong and Vice Commander Bao Chengxian fled; the rear army, seeing this, also ran, and there was a great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Degong and Vice Commander Bao Chengxian fled. The rear ranks saw them run and broke as well, and the army was routed.

sentences.zh: 渠戰死。

translations.literal: Qu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Qu died fighting.

sentences.zh: 秉忠被二刀三矢，家眾扶上馬，奪圍出，創重，卒於途。

translations.literal: Bingzhong received two sword cuts and three arrows; his household retainers helped him onto a horse, broke through the encirclement, but his wounds were grave and he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhong took two sword cuts and three arrows. His household retainers helped him onto a horse and broke through the encirclement, but his wounds were grave and he died on the road.

sentences.zh: 副將劉征擊殺十余人，乃死。

translations.literal: Vice Commander Liu Zheng struck down more than ten men and then died.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander Liu Zheng killed more than ten men before he fell.

sentences.zh: 大壽走覺華島。

translations.literal: Dashou fled to Juehua Island.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou fled to Juehua Island.

sentences.zh: 得功遂降。

translations.literal: Degong then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Degong then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 越二日，廣寧即破。

translations.literal: Two days later Guangning fell.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Guangning fell.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈一貫都督同知，世蔭副千戶；

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Yiguan was posthumously granted Vice Commissioner-in-chief of the Chief Military Commission and hereditary enfeoffment as vice chiliarch;
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, Yiguan was posthumously made Vice Commissioner of the Chief Military Commission and granted a hereditary vice chiliarch enfeoffment;

sentences.zh: 渠、秉忠少保，左都督，增世蔭三級，再蔭指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Qu and Bingzhong were granted Junior Guardian and Left Chief Commander, their families' hereditary privileges were raised three grades, and they received a second enfeoffment as battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: Qu and Bingzhong were made Junior Guardian and Left Chief Commander, their families' hereditary privileges were raised three grades, and they received a second enfeoffment as battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 皆賜祭葬，建祠並祀。

translations.literal: All were granted sacrificial rites and burial honors, and a shrine was built to sacrifice to them together.
translations.idiomatic: All were granted sacrificial rites and state burial, and a joint shrine was built in their honor.

sentences.zh: 一貫子俊傑承蔭，崇禎中仕至宣府總兵官，免歸。

translations.literal: Yiguan's son Junjie inherited the enfeoffment; during Chongzhen he served up to regional commander of Xuanfu and was dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan's son Junjie inherited the enfeoffment. During the Chongzhen reign he rose to regional commander of Xuanfu before being dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 李自成犯甘州，城陷，死之。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng attacked Ganzhou, the city fell and he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng attacked Ganzhou, the city fell and Junjie died defending it.

sentences.zh: 渠，京城巡捕營副將也，以御史楊鶴薦，擢總兵官，援剿遼東。

translations.literal: Qu had been vice commander of the Capital Patrol Battalion; on the recommendation of Censor Yang He he was promoted regional commander to relieve and suppress in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Qu had been vice commander of the Capital Patrol Battalion. On Censor Yang He's recommendation he was promoted regional commander and sent to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 遼陽被圍，廣寧總兵李光榮不能救，反斷河橋截軍民歸路，總督文球劾罷之，即以渠代。

translations.literal: When Liaoyang was besieged, Guangning regional commander Li Guangrong could not save it and instead cut the river bridge to block the return route of troops and civilians; Governor-in-chief Wen Qiu impeached and dismissed him, and Qu was appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaoyang was besieged, Guangning regional commander Li Guangrong failed to relieve it and instead cut the river bridge to block the retreat of troops and civilians. Governor-in-chief Wen Qiu impeached and dismissed him, and Qu replaced him.

sentences.zh: 西平告急，帥鎮武兵往援，遂戰歿。

translations.literal: When Xiping reported emergency, he led the Zhenwu troops to its relief and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiping sent word of emergency, he led the Zhenwu troops to its relief and died fighting.

sentences.zh: 秉忠，陜西人。

translations.literal: Bingzhong was a native of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhong was from Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年為永昌參將。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he served as assistant commander at Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 44 he served as assistant commander at Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 銀定、歹青以二千余騎入塞，秉忠提兵三百拒之，轉戰兩晝夜。

translations.literal: Yinding and Daiqing entered the frontier with more than two thousand horsemen; Bingzhong led three hundred troops to resist them and fought for two days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Yinding and Daiqing crossed the frontier with more than two thousand horsemen. Bingzhong led three hundred men against them and fought for two days and nights.

sentences.zh: 援軍至，始遁。

translations.literal: When relief troops arrived, they at last withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Only when relief troops arrived did they withdraw.

sentences.zh: 秉忠追還所掠人畜，邊人頌之。

translations.literal: Bingzhong pursued and recovered the people and livestock they had seized, and the border people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhong pursued them and recovered the people and livestock they had seized, and the border people praised him.

sentences.zh: 擢涼州副總兵。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commander-in-chief at Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commander-in-chief at Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 經略袁應泰薦其智勇，令率私卒守蒲河。

translations.literal: Commissioner Yuan Yingtai recommended his wisdom and courage and ordered him to lead his private soldiers to defend the Pu River.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Yuan Yingtai recommended his wisdom and courage and ordered him to lead his private soldiers to defend the Pu River.

sentences.zh: 至則遼陽已破，命為援剿總兵官，駐防閭陽，援西平，竟死。

translations.literal: When he arrived Liaoyang had already fallen; he was appointed relief-and-suppression regional commander, garrisoned at Lüyang, went to relieve Xiping, and in the end died.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived Liaoyang had already fallen. He was appointed relief-and-suppression regional commander, garrisoned at Lüyang, marched to relieve Xiping, and died in the end.

sentences.zh: 自遼左軍興，總兵官陣亡者凡十有四人：撫順則張承蔭，四路出師則杜松、劉綎、王宣、趙夢麟，開原則馬林，沈陽則賀世賢、尤世功，渾河則童仲揆、陳策，遼陽則楊宗業、梁仲善。

translations.literal: Since warfare arose in eastern Liaodong, regional commanders who died on the battlefield numbered fourteen in all: at Fushun, Zhang Chengyin; on the four-route advance, Du Song, Liu Ting, Wang Xuan, and Zhao Menglin; at Kaiyuan, Ma Lin; at Shenyang, He Shixian and You Shigong; at the Hun River, Tong Zhongkui and Chen Ce; at Liaoyang, Yang Zongye and Liang Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Since the war in eastern Liaodong began, fourteen regional commanders had died on the battlefield: Zhang Chengyin at Fushun; Du Song, Liu Ting, Wang Xuan, and Zhao Menglin on the four-route campaign; Ma Lin at Kaiyuan; He Shixian and You Shigong at Shenyang; Tong Zhongkui and Chen Ce at the Hun River; and Yang Zongye and Liang Zhongshan at Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 是役，渠與秉忠繼之。

translations.literal: In this campaign Qu and Bingzhong followed them.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign Qu and Bingzhong joined them.

sentences.zh: 朝端恤典，俱極優崇。

translations.literal: The court's favors and posthumous honors were all extremely generous.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted them all exceptionally generous posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 而僨軍之將，若李如柏、麻承恩輩，竟有未膺顯戮者。

translations.literal: Yet generals who had ruined the army, such as Li Rubo and Ma Chengen, in the end were not subjected to conspicuous punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet generals who had ruined their armies, such as Li Rubo and Ma Chengen, escaped conspicuous punishment.

sentences.zh: 滿桂，蒙古人，幼入中國，家宣府。

translations.literal: Man Gui was a Mongol; in youth he entered China, and his family settled in Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Man Gui was a Mongol who had entered China as a child. His family settled in Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 稍長，便騎射。

translations.literal: When he grew somewhat older he was skilled at riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up he became skilled at riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 每從征，多斬馘。

translations.literal: Whenever he followed campaigns he took many severed heads.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign after campaign he took many enemy heads.

sentences.zh: 軍令，獲敵首一，予一官，否則賚白金五十。

translations.literal: By army regulation, for one enemy head taken one office was granted; otherwise fifty taels of white silver were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Army regulations granted one office for each enemy head taken, or fifty taels of silver if no office was wanted.

sentences.zh: 桂屢得金，不受職。

translations.literal: Gui repeatedly received gold and did not accept office.
translations.idiomatic: Gui repeatedly took the silver and declined the offices.

sentences.zh: 年及壯，始為總旗。

translations.literal: When his years reached maturity he was first made company commander.
translations.idiomatic: Only when he reached maturity was he made company commander.

sentences.zh: 又十余年為百戶。

translations.literal: After more than ten years he became centurion.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years later he became centurion.

sentences.zh: 後屢遷潮河川守備。

translations.literal: Later he was repeatedly transferred as garrison commander of Chaohechuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted repeatedly until he became garrison commander of Chaohechuan.

sentences.zh: 楊鎬四路師敗，薦小將知兵者數人，首及桂。

translations.literal: When Yang Hao's four-route army was defeated, he recommended several junior officers who understood warfare, Gui being named first.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Hao's defeat on the four routes, he recommended several junior officers skilled in war, with Gui named first.

sentences.zh: 移守黃土嶺。

translations.literal: He was transferred to defend Huangtu Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to defend Huangtu Ridge.

sentences.zh: 為總督王象乾所知，進石塘路遊擊、喜峰口參將。

translations.literal: He came to the notice of Governor-in-chief Wang Xiangqian and was advanced to roaming-brigade commander on the Shitang Route and assistant commander at Xifengkou.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-in-chief Wang Xiangqian took notice of him and promoted him to roaming-brigade commander on the Shitang Route and assistant commander at Xifengkou.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，大學士孫承宗行邊，桂入謁。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi Grand Secretary Sun Chengzong toured the frontier, and Gui came to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 2 Grand Secretary Sun Chengzong toured the frontier, and Gui came to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 壯其貌，與談兵事，大奇之。

translations.literal: Chengzong admired his appearance, discussed military affairs with him, and was greatly struck by him.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong admired his bearing, talked military affairs with him, and was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 及出鎮山海，即擢副總兵，領中軍事。

translations.literal: When he went out to command Shanhai, he at once promoted him to vice commander-in-chief and put him in charge of central-army affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong took command at Shanhai, he at once promoted Gui to vice commander-in-chief and put him in charge of the central army.

sentences.zh: 承宗幕下，文武輻輳，獨用桂。

translations.literal: Under Chengzong's staff civil and military men gathered thick as spokes, yet he alone employed Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong's staff teemed with civil and military talent, yet he relied on Gui alone.

sentences.zh: 桂椎魯甚，然忠勇絕倫，不好聲色，與士卒同甘苦。

translations.literal: Gui was very blunt and rustic, yet his loyalty and courage were unmatched; he did not care for music and women and shared hardship and ease with the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was blunt and rough-spoken, but his loyalty and courage were unmatched. He cared nothing for pleasure and shared hardship and comfort with his men.

sentences.zh: 明年，承宗議出關修復寧遠。

translations.literal: The next year Chengzong discussed going beyond the pass to restore Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Chengzong proposed going beyond the pass to restore Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 問誰可守者。

translations.literal: He asked who could defend it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked who could hold it.

sentences.zh: 馬世龍薦孫諫及李承先，承宗皆不許。

translations.literal: Ma Shilong recommended Sun Jian and Li Chengxian, but Chengzong approved neither.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shilong recommended Sun Jian and Li Chengxian, but Chengzong rejected both.

sentences.zh: 袁崇煥、茅元儀進曰：「滿桂可。

translations.literal: Yuan Chonghuan and Mao Yuanyi advanced and said, "Man Gui will do."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chonghuan and Mao Yuanyi stepped forward and said, "Man Gui can do it."

sentences.zh: 但為公中軍，不敢請耳。

translations.literal: Only he is Your Lordship's central-army commander, so we did not dare request him."
translations.idiomatic: Only he is already your central-army commander, so we did not dare propose him."

sentences.zh: 」承宗曰：「既可，安問中軍。

translations.literal: " Chengzong said, "If he will do, why ask about the central army?"
translations.idiomatic: " Chengzong said, "If he will do, why ask whether he commands the central army?"

sentences.zh: 」呼桂語之，慨然請行。

translations.literal: " He called Gui and spoke to him; Gui earnestly asked to go.
translations.idiomatic: " He summoned Gui and spoke with him. Gui volunteered at once.

sentences.zh: 世龍猶疑其不可，承宗不聽。

translations.literal: Shilong still doubted it could be done, but Chengzong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong still doubted the plan, but Chengzong would not listen.

sentences.zh: 即日置酒，親為之餞。

translations.literal: That same day he set out wine and personally saw him off.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he held a farewell feast and saw him off in person.

sentences.zh: 桂至寧遠，與崇煥協心城築，屹然成重鎮。

translations.literal: Gui reached Ningyuan, and together with Chonghuan he worked in concert on wall-building until it stood firm as a great stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: Gui reached Ningyuan and, working in concert with Chonghuan, built the walls until the city stood as a major stronghold.

sentences.zh: 語具《崇煥傳》中。

translations.literal: The account is given in full in the "Biography of Chonghuan."
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the Biography of Chonghuan.

sentences.zh: 時蒙古部落駐牧寧遠東鄙，遼民來歸者悉遭劫掠，承宗患之。

translations.literal: At that time Mongol tribes pastured on the eastern marches of Ningyuan, and Liaodong people who came over to the Ming were all plundered; Chengzong was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol tribes were then pasturing on Ningyuan's eastern marches, and Liaodong people who came over to the Ming were robbed. Chengzong was troubled by this.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，遣桂及總兵尤世祿襲之大淩河。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year he sent Gui and regional commander You Shilu to strike them at the Daling River.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year four he sent Gui and regional commander You Shilu to strike them at the Daling River.

sentences.zh: 諸部號泣西竄，東鄙以寧。

translations.literal: The tribes wailed and fled westward, and the eastern marches were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes fled westward in disorder, and the eastern marches were pacified.

sentences.zh: 拱兔、炒花、宰賽諸部陽受款而陰懷反側。

translations.literal: The tribes Gongtu, Chaohua, Zaisai, and others outwardly accepted terms while inwardly harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes Gongtu, Chaohua, Zaisai, and others accepted terms in name while secretly plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 桂善操縱，諸部鹹服，歲省撫賞銀不貲。

translations.literal: Gui was skilled at managing them; all the tribes submitted, and each year uncountable sums in pacification silver were saved.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was skilled at managing them. All the tribes submitted, saving untold sums in pacification silver each year.

sentences.zh: 初，城中郭外，一望丘墟。

translations.literal: At first, within and without the city walls one saw only ruins.
translations.idiomatic: At first the city and its surroundings were nothing but ruins.

sentences.zh: 至是軍民五萬余家，屯種遠至五十里。

translations.literal: By this time more than fifty thousand military and civilian households farmed as far as fifty li away.
translations.idiomatic: By then more than fifty thousand military and civilian households were farming as far as fifty li away.

sentences.zh: 承宗上其功。

translations.literal: Chengzong reported his achievements to court.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong reported his achievements to court.

sentences.zh: 詔擢都督僉事，加銜總兵。

translations.literal: An edict promoted him to Vice Commissioner-in-chief and added the title of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him to Vice Commissioner and added the title of regional commander.

sentences.zh: 承宗乃令典後部，與前部趙率教相掎角。

translations.literal: Chengzong then put him in charge of the rear division to work in mutual support with Zhao Lujiao of the front division.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong then put him in charge of the rear division to support Zhao Lujiao's front division.

sentences.zh: 督餉郎中楊呈秀侵克軍糧，副將徐漣激之變，圍崇煥署。

translations.literal: Grain-supply supervisor Yang Chengxiu embezzled army provisions; Vice Commander Xu Lian incited a mutiny and besieged Chonghuan's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Grain-supply supervisor Yang Chengxiu embezzled army provisions. Vice Commander Xu Lian incited a mutiny and besieged Chonghuan's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 憚桂家卒勇猛，不敢犯，結隊東走。

translations.literal: They feared Gui's household retainers, who were fierce and brave, and dared not attack; they formed ranks and fled east.
translations.idiomatic: They feared Gui's fierce household retainers and dared not attack. They formed ranks and fled east.

sentences.zh: 桂與崇煥追斬首惡，撫余眾而還。

translations.literal: Gui and Chonghuan pursued them, beheaded the ringleaders, pacified the rest, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gui and Chonghuan pursued them, executed the ringleaders, pacified the rest, and returned.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，我大清以數萬騎來攻，遠邇大震，桂與崇煥死守。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year Our Great Qing came to attack with tens of thousands of horsemen; near and far were greatly shaken, and Gui and Chonghuan defended to the death.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year six the Great Qing attacked with tens of thousands of horsemen. The whole region was shaken, and Gui and Chonghuan held the city to the death.

sentences.zh: 始攻西南城隅，發西洋紅夷炮，傷攻者甚眾。

translations.literal: They first attacked the southwest corner of the wall; Western red-barbarian cannon were fired and wounded very many of the attackers.
translations.idiomatic: They first attacked the southwest corner. Western cannon were fired and inflicted heavy casualties on the attackers.

sentences.zh: 明日轉攻南城，用火器拒卻之，圍解。

translations.literal: The next day they turned to attack the south wall; firearms drove them back and the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they turned to the south wall. Firearms drove them back and the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，擢都督同知，實授總兵官。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, promoted him to Vice Commissioner-in-chief of the Chief Military Commission, and formally appointed him regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased, promoted him to Vice Commissioner of the Chief Military Commission, and formally appointed him regional commander.

sentences.zh: 再論功，加右都督，蔭副千戶，世襲。

translations.literal: When merit was discussed again, he was made Right Chief Commander, with hereditary enfeoffment as vice chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: When merit was discussed again, he was made Right Chief Commander with a hereditary vice chiliarch enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 桂疏謝，並自敘前後功。

translations.literal: Gui memorialized in thanks and also recounted his achievements before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Gui memorialized in thanks and recounted his achievements before and after.

sentences.zh: 優詔褒答，再進左都督。

translations.literal: A gracious edict praised and answered him, and he was further advanced to Left Chief Commander.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious edict praised him in reply, and he was further advanced to Left Chief Commander.

sentences.zh: 桂初與率教深相得。

translations.literal: Gui had at first been on very close terms with Lujiao.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had at first been on very close terms with Lujiao.

sentences.zh: 是役也，怒其不親救，相責望。

translations.literal: In this campaign he was angry that Lujiao had not come in person to his relief, and they reproached each other.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign he was angry that Lujiao had not come to his relief in person, and they reproached each other.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，下敕戒勉。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he issued an edict of admonition and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he issued an edict admonishing and encouraging them.

sentences.zh: 而崇煥復與桂不和，言其意氣驕矜，謾罵僚屬，恐壞封疆大計，乞移之別鎮，以關外事權歸率教。

translations.literal: But Chonghuan was again at odds with Gui, saying he was proud and overbearing, reviled his colleagues, and might ruin the great plan for the frontier; he begged to transfer him to another command so that authority over affairs beyond the pass would return to Lujiao.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghuan was again at odds with Gui, saying he was proud and overbearing, abused his colleagues, and might ruin frontier strategy. He asked to transfer Gui elsewhere so that authority beyond the pass would return to Lujiao.

sentences.zh: 舉朝皆知桂可用，慮同城或僨事，遂召還。

translations.literal: The whole court knew Gui could be used, but feared that sharing a city might ruin affairs, and so he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court knew Gui was valuable but feared that sharing one city might ruin affairs, and so he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 督師王之臣力言桂不可去，而召命已下。

translations.literal: Supreme Commander Wang Zhichen strongly argued that Gui must not leave, but the recall order had already been issued.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Commander Wang Zhichen strongly argued that Gui must not leave, but the recall order had already been issued.

sentences.zh: 又請用之關門。

translations.literal: He again asked that Gui be used at Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked that Gui be used at Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 崇煥皆不納。

translations.literal: Chonghuan would accept none of it.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghuan rejected all of it.

sentences.zh: 閏六月乃命以故秩僉書中軍府事。

translations.literal: In the intercalary sixth month he was ordered to serve in the Central Military Commission at his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary sixth month he was ordered to serve in the Central Military Commission at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 未幾，崇煥亦自悔，請仍用之臣言，帝可之，命桂掛印移鎮關門，兼統關外四路及燕河、建昌諸軍，賜尚方劍以重事權。

translations.literal: Before long Chonghuan also repented and asked that Zhichen's words still be followed; the emperor approved, ordered Gui to take his seal and transfer command to Shanhaiguan, concurrently commanding the four routes beyond the pass and the armies of Yanhe, Jianchang, and elsewhere, and bestowed the Imperial Sword to weight his authority.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chonghuan repented as well and asked that Zhichen's advice be followed. The emperor approved, ordered Gui to transfer to Shanhaiguan with his seal, gave him command over the four routes beyond the pass and the armies of Yanhe, Jianchang, and elsewhere, and bestowed the Imperial Sword to strengthen his authority.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，大清兵圍錦州，分兵略寧遠。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year Qing troops besieged Jinzhou and sent detachments to threaten Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year seven Qing troops besieged Jinzhou and sent detachments against Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 桂遣兵救，被圍笊籬山。

translations.literal: Gui sent troops to the relief, but they were besieged at Zhaoli Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Gui sent troops to the relief, but they were besieged at Zhaoli Mountain.

sentences.zh: 桂與總兵尤世祿赴之，大戰相當。

translations.literal: Gui and regional commander You Shilu went to their aid and fought a great battle on even terms.
translations.idiomatic: Gui and regional commander You Shilu went to their aid and fought a fierce, even battle.

sentences.zh: 遂入寧遠城，與崇煥為守禦計。

translations.literal: He then entered Ningyuan city and with Chonghuan made plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered Ningyuan and with Chonghuan planned the defense.

sentences.zh: 俄大清兵進薄城下，桂率副將尤世威等出城迎，頗有殺傷，桂亦身被重創。

translations.literal: Presently Qing troops pressed close below the walls; Gui led Vice Commanders You Shiwei and others out to meet them, inflicted considerable killing and wounding, and Gui himself received grave wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qing troops pressed close below the walls. Gui led Vice Commanders You Shiwei and others out to meet them, inflicted heavy casualties, and was himself gravely wounded.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，加太子太師，世蔭錦衣僉事。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, with hereditary enfeoffment as commissioner of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, he was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent with a hereditary enfeoffment in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 及崇煥休去，之臣再督師，盛推桂才，請仍鎮寧遠。

translations.literal: When Chonghuan took leave and departed, Zhichen again became supreme commander, greatly praised Gui's talent, and asked that he still command at Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Chonghuan took leave, Zhichen again became supreme commander, praised Gui's talent highly, and asked that he remain at Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 會蒙古炒花諸部離散，桂與之臣多收置之麾下。

translations.literal: It happened that the Mongol tribes Chaohua and others had scattered; Gui and Zhichen took many of them into their commands.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol tribes Chaohua and others had scattered, and Gui and Zhichen took many of them into their commands.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝已嗣位，詔之臣毋蹈袁應泰、王化貞故轍，並責桂阿之臣意。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuanglie had already succeeded to the throne; he ordered Zhichen not to follow the old tracks of Yuan Yingtai and Wang Huazhen, and also reproached Gui for flattering Zhichen's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuanglie had already ascended the throne. He ordered Zhichen not to repeat the mistakes of Yuan Yingtai and Wang Huazhen and also reproached Gui for flattering Zhichen.

sentences.zh: 桂遂請病乞休，不允。

translations.literal: Gui then asked leave on grounds of illness, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Gui then asked to retire on grounds of illness, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年七月，言官交劾之臣，因及桂。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Chongzhen censors impeached Zhichen in succession, and Gui was implicated.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Chongzhen 1 censors impeached Zhichen in succession and implicated Gui as well.

sentences.zh: 之臣罷，桂亦召還府。

translations.literal: Zhichen was dismissed, and Gui was also recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhichen was dismissed, and Gui was recalled to the capital as well.

sentences.zh: 適大同總兵渠家楨失事，命桂代之。

translations.literal: It happened that Datong regional commander Qu Jiazhen had failed in his post, and Gui was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Datong regional commander Qu Jiazhen had just failed in his post, and Gui was ordered to replace him.

sentences.zh: 大同久恃款弛備，插部西侵，順義王遂入境大掠。

translations.literal: Datong had long relied on peace agreements and relaxed its defenses; the Chahar tribe invaded from the west, and the Shunyi King then entered the territory and ravaged on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Datong had long relied on peace agreements and let its defenses lapse. The Chahar invaded from the west, and the Shunyi King swept in and ravaged the region.

sentences.zh: 家楨及巡撫張翼明論死，插部遂挾賞不去。

translations.literal: Jiazhen and Grand Coordinator Zhang Yiming were sentenced to death; the Chahar then held out for rewards and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen and Grand Coordinator Zhang Yiming were sentenced to death. The Chahar then held out for rewards and refused to leave.

sentences.zh: 桂至，遍閱八路七十二城堡，邊備大修，軍民恃以無恐。

translations.literal: When Gui arrived, he inspected all seventy-two fortresses of the eight routes; frontier defenses were greatly restored, and military and civilians relied on him without fear.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui arrived, he inspected all seventy-two fortresses of the eight routes, greatly restored the frontier defenses, and gave soldiers and civilians confidence again.

sentences.zh: 明年冬十月，大清兵入近畿。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the following winter Qing troops entered the near capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the following winter Qing troops entered the capital region.

sentences.zh: 十一月詔諭勤王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month an edict summoned troops to relieve the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month an edict summoned troops to relieve the throne.

sentences.zh: 桂率五千騎入衛，次順義，與宣府總兵侯世祿俱戰敗，遂趨都城。

translations.literal: Gui led five thousand horsemen to the capital's defense, halted at Shunyi, and together with Xuanfu regional commander Hou Shilu was defeated in battle, then hurried to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Gui led five thousand horsemen to the capital's defense, halted at Shunyi, was defeated together with Xuanfu regional commander Hou Shilu, and then hurried to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝遣官慰勞，犒萬金，令與世祿俱屯德勝門。

translations.literal: The emperor sent officials to comfort and reward him with ten thousand taels of gold, and ordered him to garrison at Desheng Gate together with Shilu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent officials to comfort him, rewarded him with ten thousand taels of gold, and ordered him to garrison at Desheng Gate together with Shilu.

sentences.zh: 無何，合戰，世祿兵潰，桂獨前鬥。

translations.literal: Before long they joined battle; Shilu's troops were routed, and Gui alone pressed forward to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they joined battle. Shilu's troops broke, and Gui alone pressed forward to fight.

sentences.zh: 城上發大炮佐之，誤傷桂軍，桂亦負傷，令入休甕城。

translations.literal: Cannon were fired from the walls to assist him, but mistakenly wounded Gui's army; Gui was also wounded and ordered to rest in the barbican.
translations.idiomatic: Cannon on the walls fired to assist him but mistakenly struck Gui's own men. Gui was wounded as well and ordered to rest in the barbican.

sentences.zh: 旋與袁崇煥、祖大壽並召見，桂解衣示創，帝深嘉嘆。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned together with Yuan Chonghuan and Zu Dashou; Gui removed his garment to show his wounds, and the emperor greatly praised and sighed over him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned together with Yuan Chonghuan and Zu Dashou. Gui removed his garment to show his wounds, and the emperor praised him deeply.

sentences.zh: 十二月朔復召見，下崇煥獄，賜桂酒饌，令總理關、寧將卒，營安定門外。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month he was summoned again; Chonghuan was cast into prison, wine and food were bestowed on Gui, and he was ordered to take overall command of the Shanhai and Ningyuan troops and encamp outside Anding Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month he was summoned again. Chonghuan was imprisoned, wine and food were bestowed on Gui, and he was ordered to take overall command of the Shanhai and Ningyuan troops and encamp outside Anding Gate.

sentences.zh: 桂驍勇敢戰。

translations.literal: Gui was fierce and brave in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was fierce and brave in battle.

sentences.zh: 所部降丁間擾民，桂不能問。

translations.literal: Surrendered tribesmen under his command sometimes harassed the people, and Gui could not investigate them.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered tribesmen under his command sometimes harassed civilians, and Gui could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 副將申甫所統多市人，桂軍淩之。

translations.literal: Vice Commander Shen Fu commanded mostly townspeople, and Gui's troops bullied them.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander Shen Fu commanded mostly townspeople, and Gui's troops bullied them.

sentences.zh: 夜發矢，驚其營，有死者。

translations.literal: At night they shot arrows, startling their camp, and some were killed.
translations.idiomatic: At night they shot arrows into the camp, causing panic and killing some men.

sentences.zh: 御史金聲以聞，帝亦不問。

translations.literal: Censor Jin Sheng reported it, but the emperor also did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Jin Sheng reported it, but the emperor did not inquire.

sentences.zh: 及大壽軍東潰，乃拜桂武經略，盡統入衛諸軍，賜尚方劍，趣出師。

translations.literal: When Dashou's army collapsed eastward, Gui was appointed Military Commissioner and given overall command of all troops that had entered to guard the capital; the Imperial Sword was bestowed and he was urged to march out.
translations.idiomatic: When Dashou's army collapsed to the east, Gui was appointed Military Commissioner, given overall command of all troops that had come to guard the capital, bestowed the Imperial Sword, and urged to march out.

sentences.zh: 桂曰：「敵勁援寡，未可輕戰。

translations.literal: Gui said, "The enemy is strong and relief few—we must not fight lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, "The enemy is strong and our reinforcements few. We must not fight rashly."

sentences.zh: 」中使趣之急，不得已，督黑雲龍、麻登雲、孫祖壽諸大將，以十五日移營永定門外二里許，列柵以待。

translations.literal: " Palace envoys pressed him urgently; having no choice, he supervised the great generals Hei Yunlong, Ma Dengyun, Sun Zushou, and others, and on the fifteenth day moved camp about two li outside Yongding Gate, set up palisades, and waited.
translations.idiomatic: " Palace envoys pressed him urgently. Having no choice, he supervised the great generals Hei Yunlong, Ma Dengyun, Sun Zushou, and others and on the fifteenth day moved camp about two li outside Yongding Gate, set up palisades, and waited.

sentences.zh: 大清兵自良鄉回，明日昧爽，以精騎四面蹙之。

translations.literal: Qing troops returned from Liangxiang; at dawn the next day elite cavalry pressed in on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Qing troops returned from Liangxiang. At dawn the next day elite cavalry closed in on every side.

sentences.zh: 諸將不能支，大敗，桂及祖壽戰死，雲龍、登雲被執。

translations.literal: The generals could not hold; there was a great defeat; Gui and Zushou died in battle, and Yunlong and Dengyun were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The generals could not hold. The army was routed. Gui and Zushou died fighting, and Yunlong and Dengyun were captured.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，震悼，遣禮部侍郎徐光啟致祭，贈少師，世蔭錦衣僉事，襲升三級，賜祭葬，有司建祠。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he was shaken and grieved; Vice Minister of Rites Xu Guangqi was sent to perform the sacrifice; Gui was posthumously granted Junior Guardian, hereditary enfeoffment as commissioner of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, three grades of advancement by succession, sacrificial rites and burial honors, and the relevant offices built a shrine.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he was shaken with grief. Vice Minister of Rites Xu Guangqi was sent to perform the sacrifice. Gui was posthumously made Junior Guardian, granted a hereditary enfeoffment in the Embroidered Uniform Guard and three grades of advancement by succession, and given sacrificial rites and state burial. The relevant offices built a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 孫祖壽，字必之，昌平人。

translations.literal: Sun Zushou, style Bizhi, was a native of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zushou, style Bizhi, was from Changping.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中舉武鄉試，授固關把總。

translations.literal: During Wanli he passed the military provincial examination and was appointed platoon leader at Guguan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he passed the military provincial examination and was appointed platoon leader at Guguan.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年歷官署都督僉事，為薊鎮總兵官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he rose through offices to Acting Vice Commissioner-in-chief and became regional commander of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 2 he rose to Acting Vice Commissioner and became regional commander of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 孫承宗行邊，議於薊鎮三協十二路分設三大將。

translations.literal: When Sun Chengzong toured the frontier, he proposed that the three commands and twelve routes of Jizhou be divided among three great generals.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Chengzong toured the frontier, he proposed dividing Jizhou's three commands and twelve routes among three great generals.

sentences.zh: 以祖壽領西協，轄石匣、古北、曹家、墻子四路，駐遵化。

translations.literal: Zushou was put in charge of the western command, governing the four routes of Shixia, Gubei, Caojia, and Qiangzi, stationed at Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: Zushou was put in charge of the western command, governing the four routes of Shixia, Gubei, Caojia, and Qiangzi from Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 而江應詔領東協，駐關門，轄山海關、一片石、燕河、建昌四路。

translations.literal: Jiang Ying'e commanded the eastern command, stationed at Shanhaiguan, governing the four routes of Shanhaiguan, Yipianshi, Yanhe, and Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ying'e commanded the eastern command from Shanhaiguan, governing the four routes of Shanhaiguan, Yipianshi, Yanhe, and Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 馬世龍領中協，駐三屯營，轄馬蘭、松棚、喜峰、太平四路。

translations.literal: Ma Shilong commanded the central command, stationed at Santun Camp, governing the four routes of Malan, Songpeng, Xifeng, and Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shilong commanded the central command from Santun Camp, governing the four routes of Malan, Songpeng, Xifeng, and Taiping.

sentences.zh: 經略王在晉、總督王象乾僉謂：「永平設鎮，本以衛山海。

translations.literal: Commissioner Wang Zaijin and Governor-in-chief Wang Xiangqian jointly said, "Yongping was made a command post originally to guard Shanhai."
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Wang Zaijin and Governor-in-chief Wang Xiangqian jointly said, "Yongping was originally made a command post to guard Shanhai."

sentences.zh: 今移之三屯，則去山海四百里，於應援為疏。

translations.literal: " Now if it is moved to Santun, it is four hundred li from Shanhai, which makes relief too distant."
translations.idiomatic: " Moving it to Santun puts it four hundred li from Shanhai, which makes relief too distant."

sentences.zh: 遵化去三屯止六十里，今並列兩鎮，於建牙為贅。

translations.literal: " Zunhua is only sixty li from Santun; now to set up two command posts side by side is redundant in establishing headquarters."
translations.idiomatic: " Zunhua is only sixty li from Santun. Setting up two command posts side by side is redundant."

sentences.zh: 請令世龍仍鎮永平，以東協四路分隸世龍、應詔，而以中、西二協專隸之祖壽，仍鎮三屯。

translations.literal: " We ask that Shilong still command at Yongping, that the four routes of the eastern command be divided between Shilong and Ying'e, and that the central and western commands be placed solely under Zushou, who should still command at Santun."
